examples.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions Using the Product or Quotient Rule
examples.worked_solution:
Applying the product rule and using the formula for the derivative of $\arccos x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) & =x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)+\operatorname{arccos}⁡x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\cdot (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}})+\operatorname{arccos}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}+\operatorname{arccos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(5{x}^{3})] \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{(5{x}^{3})}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+25{x}^{6}}\cdot 15{x}^{2} \\  & =\frac{15{x}^{2}}{1+25{x}^{6}}.\end{aligned}
$$
